questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience a culture I was not familiar with in the slightest, that's the reason why an Asian country seemed like a good option.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival, I was quite confused and overwhelmed but once classes started I found most of the information I needed through talking with fellow students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance once I arrived in South Korea, which perhaps made the first couple of weeks more complicated, but I managed to find all the information I needed by myself and through other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was satisfactory but maybe not as thorough as what I was expecting.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy but I managed to find a room on AirBnB and get a signed contract from my landlord which allowed me to stay there during the entire semester.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Future exchange students should know that living off campus is completely fine as long as you're in the general area of Sillim/SNU station.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: From what I gathered, it seems that only a limited number of exchange students were able to get a room on campus and the majority of us had to find other housing options off campus without any assistance from our host university. I was not pleased with this as it was just an unnecessary source f anxiety during an already stressful period.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Course registration was straight-forward and the guidelines provided were helpful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration is done on a website where you can pick courses you are interested in, add them to your cart and then eventually select them. The only downside is that it's a first-come first-served basis.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online resources showed every step of the process in ample detail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was more or less successful in registering for the classes I wanted. The only issue was that a class I wanted to take was offered at a different campus so I had to replace it with another one.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure not to miss the deadlines!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two BA level courses and two MA level courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I was taking four courses simultaneously which all ran for the entire semester, something that differed quite a bit from the block system I got used to back at UCPH. The style of teaching itself was not too different, it mostly consisted in lectures, presentations and course work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Artificial Intelligence for New Drug Development and Clinical Application
- Theory and Practice in Computational Sciences 2
- Seminar in Oceanography
- Korean History

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't think I have any courses I would recommend.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive than what I expected, especially fruits and dairy products. Eating out and public transportation were cheaper than what I was expecting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most clubs and sports at SNU are not open to foreigners.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Social activities for students are frequent if you are part of the SNU buddy programme but I was not. For cultural, athletic and social activities, I did not rely on anything organised by my host university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Jogging and hiking are easy ways to exercise as an exchange student because they don't require joining any club or association. For cultural activities, Seoul has a lot to offer in terms of museums and exhibitions.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Seoul is the perfect city to go out and that is how I spent a lot of weekends. There's also a lot of nice destinations to go on weekend trips like Seoraksan national park, Jeju island and more.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I did not find it too hard to adjust to the local culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Socialising with local students is very difficult, the best way to do so is to speak Korean.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I starting missing European food after the first few months in Korea and it's been a bit of a challenge sometimes. But nothing too serious.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really liked how full of life Seoul is and how Koreans are always willing to have fun, eat good food and socialise.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Consider joining the SNU buddy programme (I didn't and missed out on a lot of social events).
2. Learn Hangul (the Korean alphabet) and join a Korean class.
3. Take some time off whenever you can to travel around Korea or to neighbouring countries.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't expect to find housing on campus.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning the basics of Korean, making friends from all over the world, feeling at home in a city that used to feel so far away and different.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Loneliness was sometimes hard to deal with.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
